# Accessible component library

> Accessible UI components as folders of plain files — no build step, no dependencies. Read them, copy them, adapt them.

Markup that resembles an ARIA pattern is the easy part. Which attribute the browser ignores, which
state cue vanishes in Windows High Contrast, which focus move a screen reader never announces — that
is what this library hands over.

## Read in this order

Tier 0 is this file. Relative paths resolve against it; a `<slug>` comes from the index.

- [agents/index.md](https://kaseycolian.github.io/a11y-component-examples/agents/index.md) — tier 1, 3.2 KB. The roster. Find your component, then stop reading this file.
- [agents/index.json](https://kaseycolian.github.io/a11y-component-examples/agents/index.json) — tier 1, 15.6 KB. Every field, for filtering by tag or SC.
- `library/components/<slug>/component.{html,css,js}` — tier 3, varies. The code. Copy from here.
- `library/components/<slug>/{docs.md,meta.json}` — tier 4, varies. Why it is built that way. Read when the code surprises you.

## Rules

**Read down the path.** Each tier names the next; stop at the one that answered you.

**Never read `docs/BUILD-STATUS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`** — a build log and a style guide, tens of thousands
of tokens for nothing about accessibility. `docs/` is for people working *on* the library.

**The files are the answer.** Copy from `component.html`, `component.css` and `component.js`, not from
anything written about them.

**Deliberate failures are labeled.** Most components ship a broken example so the difference is
visible; anything carrying `data-ac-demo-broken` is wrong by design. Never copy from inside one.

## What a copied component needs

Each component stands alone: CSS scoped to `.ac-<slug>`, an IIFE registering `window.AC.create<Name>`
returning `destroy()`, no imports. Pasting the files into a bare page works.

Three conventions fail silently if stripped. Every color is
`var(--ac-token, var(--theme-token, #literal))` — flatten it and the component stops following its
host theme. Every component ends with `@media (forced-colors: active)` — High Contrast drops
`color-mix`, shadows and tinted fills, which is where state cues live. Transitions are gated through
`calc(var(--ac-motion, var(--motion, 1)) * …)` so `prefers-reduced-motion` reaches them.

No component for what you need? The nearest one still earns the read: the ARIA is pattern-specific,
the traps are not.
